div.head: ECf retr Inscr.

ab.hi: Incipiunt leges Edwardi regis, quas Willelmus postea confirmauit (in Anglia).

div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 627 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.
Liebermann’s note a, on ECf as a whole and on the Retractator and his manuscripts, is printed under the ECf column; it is given here as well.
There is no note 3 on this page in the ECf retr column: Liebermann’s numbering goes from 2 to 4.

note.seg: Vgl. mein Über Leges Edwardi Conf. Halle 1896. — Verfasser steht der Sprache, Literatur und Verfassung der Angelsachsen ferner und hierarchischem Anspruch des 12. Jhs. näher als In. Cn., Cons. Cn. oder Quadr. und Hn. Er kennt den Wechsel des Besitzes an gewissen Gütern um 1093 bis 1115 oder 1130; er grollt über ein Ereigniss von 1096, wohl als selbsterlebt; Stephans Zugeständnisse 1135/36 benutzt er nicht. Er kennt vielleicht Warwickshire. Hss.: Rl um 1190; Hk (wovon Ed 2 abhängt) Cl Hr spl (Vorlage für Pl und S, dem Vl folgt) und die 34, 1a endende Classe adow, der zugehören Ad (um 1210) Do No Ck und Wo, die Vorlage für Ed 1. Der Retractator, jüngerer Zeitgenoss jenes, schreibt (vielleicht in Kent) vor 1159. — Sein Werk steht nur in der Tripartita [d. h. hinter Wl art und vor der Genealogia Normann., zwei Werken anderer Verfasser. Die Genealogia, von 1136—54 (edirt von mir Über Ed. Conf. S. 134) stammt vielleicht vom Tripartita-Sammler.] Hss.: Cb um 1160, Dc Sp Oh Lm Wi Ar pehy, die Vorlage von Pe Hy; ferner die Hss. mit den Überschriften des Rubricator II, nach 1154, nämlich Ld 1 Cu Hv L Db Hunt-Anhang (dem zugehören Lb um 1200, rv [Vorlage von Ra Vi; vgl. Wl art. Inscr.¹] Gr Rc Va La Ba Ph Kn und Lond, d. i. Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Lond. coll. [vgl. deren Edition von mir S. 38—64] in K Co (woraus Ld 2 schöpfte) Or und Ce, d. i. einer Lichfielder Chronik 14. Jhs. — Aus ECf. und ECf. retr. mengt den Text Ce, womit in Londons Guildhall Horn und Liber memor. (vgl. S. 633¹⁰) stimmen. Überschriften des Rubricator II setzt zu ECf. Classe spl.

Cf. my Über Leges Edwardi Conf., Halle 1896. — The author stands further from the language, literature and constitution of the Anglo-Saxons, and closer to the hierarchical claims of the 12th century, than In. Cn., Cons. Cn. or Quadr. and Hn. He knows of the change of ownership of certain estates around 1093 to 1115 or 1130; he is aggrieved at an event of 1096, probably as one he lived through; he does not use Stephen’s concessions of 1135/36. He perhaps knows Warwickshire. MSS: Rl c. 1190; Hk (on which Ed 2 depends) Cl Hr spl (the exemplar of Pl and S, which Vl follows) and the class adow, which ends at 34, 1a, to which belong Ad (c. 1210) Do No Ck and Wo, the exemplar of Ed 1. The Retractator, a younger contemporary of that author, writes (perhaps in Kent) before 1159. — His work stands only in the Tripartita [i.e. after Wl art and before the Genealogia Normann., two works by other authors. The Genealogia, of 1136–54 (edited by me, Über Ed. Conf. p. 134), perhaps comes from the compiler of the Tripartita.] MSS: Cb c. 1160, Dc Sp Oh Lm Wi Ar pehy, the exemplar of Pe Hy; further the MSS with the headings of Rubricator II, after 1154, namely Ld 1 Cu Hv L Db Hunt-Anhang (to which belong Lb c. 1200, rv [the exemplar of Ra Vi; cf. Wl art. Inscr.¹] Gr Rc Va La Ba Ph Kn and Lond, i.e. Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Lond. coll. [cf. my edition of it, pp. 38–64] in K Co (from which Ld 2 drew) Or and Ce, i.e. a Lichfield chronicle of the 14th century. — Ce mixes its text from ECf. and ECf. retr.; London’s Guildhall Horn and Liber memor. (cf. p. 633¹⁰) agree with it. Class spl adds the headings of Rubricator II to ECf.
